title: Unscaled residue differential basis and a residue inverse after adjoining one unit
statement: Let k be a field of characteristic p > 0, Λ a Noetherian k-algebra [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], q a prime ideal, n ≥ 1, L = Λ_q [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], J = qL, B = L/J^n, and π : Λ → B the canonical map. Let A₀ ⊆ B be an admissible local k-subalgebra [def-weil-pbc-popescu-admissible-subalgebra]. Let a₀ : Fin t₀ → A₀ and let b₀ be an F₀-basis of Ω[F₀/k] [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials], where F₀ is the residue field of A₀, such that b₀ j = d(residue_A₀(a₀ j)). Let s ∈ Λ \ q. There exist an admissible local k-subalgebra A ⊆ B and an inclusion hle : A₀ ≤ A, an integer Q ≥ 1, a unit z ∈ A× with (z π(s)^Q - 1) nilpotent in B, an integer m ≥ 0, elements y : Fin m → A whose images in B all equal π(s), and a basis b of Ω[F/k] over the residue field F of A indexed by Fin t₀ ⊕ Fin m. For each j in Fin t₀, b(inl j) = d(residue_A(inclusion_hle(a₀ j))); for each j in Fin m, b(inr j) = d(residue_A(y j)). There is no numerator family, no actual denominator power in A, and no basis lifted from Λ in this statement.

proof.text: Write L = Λ_q, J = qL, B = L/J^n. As n ≥ 1, B is Artinian local, with maximal ideal JB and nilpotence exponent n. The admissibility identity m₀B = m_B identifies m₀ with A₀ ∩ m_B, so the residue field F₀ embeds into K. The element s maps to a unit x, and α = residue_B(x) is nonzero. The given basis b₀ identifies dc_j as a basis of Ω[F₀/k]; the given basis and its lifts are hypotheses, so no numerator or denominator selection is needed here. The residue field F₀ is essentially of finite type over k as a quotient of A₀, hence is finitely generated as a field over k.

proof.text: Let α be the nonzero residue of x in K. If α is transcendental over F₀, perform the polynomial localization construction below. If it is algebraic, choose a positive p-power Q such that β = α^Q is separable over F₀ and perform the finite étale construction below. In either case the required output before clearing denominators is an admissible A containing A₀, a unit z with z x^Q - 1 nilpotent, and a basis consisting of the original residue differentials and, only in the transcendental case, dα. No numerator family or power of x in A is asserted here.

proof.text: *Case T: the ring $D'$ (as in 07FI, case transcendental).* Let $\theta:A_0[t]\to\bar\Lambda$ be the $A_0$-algebra map with $t\mapsto\bar s$ and $\mathfrak n=\theta^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak m})$. Since $A_0\subseteq\bar\Lambda$ is local, $\mathfrak m_{A_0}[t]\subseteq\mathfrak n$, and modulo $\mathfrak m_{A_0}[t]$ the map $A_0[t]\to K$ is $F_0[t]\to K$, $t\mapsto\alpha$, which is injective as $\alpha$ is transcendental over $F_0$; so $\mathfrak n=\mathfrak m_{A_0}[t]$, a prime ideal ($A_0[t]/\mathfrak n=F_0[t]$ is a domain). Let $D'=A_0[t]_{\mathfrak n}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. $A_0[t]$ is Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian] and so is $D'$ [lem-weil-pbc-localization-noetherian]. $D'/\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'=(F_0[t])_{(0)}=F_0(t)$ is a field and $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$ is nilpotent ($\mathfrak m_{A_0}$ is, step 1), so $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$ lies in every prime of $D'$ and is the maximal ideal of the local ring $D'$; $D'$ is Artinian local [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] (with $K=0$ there), with residue field $F_0(t)$, and $A_0\to D'$ is local. Every element of $A_0[t]\setminus\mathfrak n$ maps outside $\bar{\mathfrak m}$, i.e. to a unit of $\bar\Lambda$, so $\theta$ extends to $\psi':D'\to\bar\Lambda$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], local ($\psi'^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak m})=\mathfrak nD'$), restricting to the inclusion on $A_0$, with $\psi'(t/1)=\bar s$; on residue fields it is $F_0(t)\to K$, $t\mapsto\alpha$.

proof.text: *Case T: $A=\psi'(D')$ is admissible.* Apply [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] to $R=A_0$, $S=D'$, $S'=M=\bar\Lambda$: Noetherian local rings (steps 1, 3) and local homomorphisms; $M$ is generated by $1$ and nonzero; $M/\mathfrak m_{A_0}M$ is a vector space over the field $D'/\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$, hence free and flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; $M$ is flat over $A_0$ ($A_0$ admissible). So $\psi'$ is flat; being local it is faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] and so injective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction] ($I=0$). Let $A=\psi'(D')\cong D'$, a $k$-subalgebra of $\bar\Lambda$ containing $A_0=\psi'(A_0)$ and $\bar s$: it is Artinian local, $A\to\bar\Lambda$ is flat, and $\mathfrak m_A\bar\Lambda=\mathfrak m_{A_0}\bar\Lambda=\bar{\mathfrak m}$. Its residue field $F\subseteq K$ is the image of $F_0(t)$, i.e. $F=F_0(\alpha)\cong F_0(t)$ ($t\mapsto\alpha$), finitely generated over $k$ (by $\alpha$ and generators of $F_0$ from the initial setup). Writing $F=k(e_1,\dots,e_v)$, $F=W^{-1}k[e_1,\dots,e_v]$ with $W$ the nonzero elements of the domain $k[e_1,\dots,e_v]$, so $k\to F$ is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra], and by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-essentially-finite-type-residue] $A$ is essentially of finite type over $k$. So $A$ is admissible, $A_0\subseteq A$, $\bar s\in A$. Since the maximal ideal of A is the contraction of the ambient maximal ideal, x is a unit of A. Take Q = 1 and z = x⁻¹. Then z x^Q - 1 = 0 is nilpotent.

proof.text: *Case T: a basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$.* By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-polynomial-extension] ($R=k$, $A=F_0$, $e=1$) $\Omega_{F_0[t]/k}\cong(F_0[t]\otimes_{F_0}\Omega_{F_0/k})\oplus F_0[t]\,\mathrm dt$ via $b\otimes\mathrm dc\mapsto b\,\mathrm dc$; as $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t$ is an $F_0$-basis of $\Omega_{F_0/k}$ , $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t,\mathrm dt$ is an $F_0[t]$-basis of $\Omega_{F_0[t]/k}$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. $F_0(t)$ is the localization of $F_0[t]$ at its nonzero elements, so by [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-localization] $\Omega_{F_0(t)/k}$ is the localization of $\Omega_{F_0[t]/k}$ and $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t,\mathrm dt$ is an $F_0(t)$-basis of it. Transporting along the $k$-algebra isomorphism $F_0(t)\cong F$, $t\mapsto\alpha$, identity on $F_0$, $\mathrm dc_1,\dots,\mathrm dc_t,\mathrm d\alpha$ is an $F$-basis of $\Omega_{F/k}$.

proof.text: *Case S: the field $F_1=F_0(\beta)$ (as in 07FI, case algebraic).* $\alpha$ is algebraic over $F_0$, so $F_0(\alpha)/F_0$ is an algebraic extension and by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable] there is $Q=p^e$ ($e\ge0$) with $\beta:=\alpha^Q$ separable over $F_0$ [def-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-extension]; $\beta\neq0$. Let $F_1=F_0(\beta)\subseteq K$; it is generated by $\beta$, so $F_1\cong F_0[T]/(\bar g)$, $\bar g$ the minimal polynomial of $\beta$, is finite over $F_0$, and as the elements of $F_1$ separable over $F_0$ form a subfield containing $F_0$ and $\beta$ [lem-weil-pbc-separable-first-purely-inseparable], $F_1/F_0$ is finite and separable algebraic. Hence $F_1$ is a finite etale $F_0$-algebra, by Algebra.Etale.of_finite_of_isSeparable [lem-weil-pbc-finite-separable-extension-etale]. $A_0$ and $\bar\Lambda$ are local rings whose only prime is the maximal ideal [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime], have nilpotent maximal ideals and hence are henselian [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-of-nil-maximal-ideal]. By the essential surjectivity in [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-finite-etale-equivalence] for $A_0$ and the finite etale $F_0$-algebra $F_1$ there is a finite etale $A_0$-algebra $D'$ with an $F_0$-algebra isomorphism $D'/\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'\cong F_1$. $D'$ is finite over $A_0$, hence Noetherian [lem-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra-noetherian]; $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$ is nilpotent with quotient a field, so it is the maximal ideal of the local ring $D'$, which is Artinian [lem-weil-pbc-noetherian-local-quotient-artinian-local] with residue field $F_1$, and $A_0\to D'$ is local.

proof.text: *Case S: a factorization $A_0\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ (Stacks: 'since $\bar\Lambda$ is henselian and $F(\alpha^q)$ is contained in its residue field we can find a factorization').* Let $\rho:D'\to F_1\subseteq K$ be the residue map composed with the isomorphism above; on $A_0$ it is the residue map $A_0\to F_0\subseteq K$. Let $C=D'\otimes_{A_0}\bar\Lambda$; $\bar\Lambda\to C$, $x\mapsto1\otimes x$, is etale [lem-weil-pbc-etale-ring-base-change]. The maps $\rho$ and $x\mapsto\hat x$ are ring maps $D'\to K$, $\bar\Lambda\to K$ agreeing on $A_0$, so they define a ring map $\chi:C\to K$, $d\otimes x\mapsto\rho(d)\hat x$, surjective (already on $1\otimes\bar\Lambda$). Its kernel $\mathfrak q'$ is a prime of $C$ lying over $\bar{\mathfrak m}$, and $K=\bar\Lambda/\bar{\mathfrak m}\to C/\mathfrak q'\cong K$ is the identity, an isomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-henselian-etale-retraction] ($\bar\Lambda$ henselian by the preceding construction) there is a $\bar\Lambda$-algebra map $\sigma:C\to\bar\Lambda$ with $\sigma^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak m})=\mathfrak q'$. Put $\psi'(d)=\sigma(d\otimes1)$. For $a\in A_0$, $\psi'(a)=\sigma(1\otimes a)=a$, so $\psi'$ restricts to the inclusion on $A_0$. Reducing $\sigma$ modulo $\bar{\mathfrak m}$ gives a $K$-algebra map $C/\mathfrak q'\to K$, which is the inverse of the isomorphism $K\to C/\mathfrak q'$; hence $\widehat{\psi'(d)}=\chi(d\otimes1)=\rho(d)$ for $d\in D'$. So $\psi'$ is local ($\psi'^{-1}(\bar{\mathfrak m})$ is a prime of $D'$, i.e. $\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'$, by [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-unique-prime]) and induces on residue fields the inclusion $F_1\subseteq K$.

proof.text: *Case S: $A=\psi'(D')$ is admissible and a residue inverse.* As in the transcendental case, [lem-weil-pbc-criterion-flatness-fibre-noetherian] for $A_0\to D'\to\bar\Lambda$ and $M=\bar\Lambda$ ($M/\mathfrak m_{A_0}M$ is a vector space over the field $D'/\mathfrak m_{A_0}D'\cong F_1$, hence flat [def-weil-pbc-flat-ring-map]; $M$ flat over $A_0$) shows that $\psi'$ is flat; it is local, hence faithfully flat [lem-weil-pbc-flat-local-hom-faithfully-flat] and injective [lem-weil-pbc-faithfully-flat-ideal-contraction]. $A=\psi'(D')\cong D'$ is a $k$-subalgebra of $\bar\Lambda$ containing $A_0$, Artinian local, flat into $\bar\Lambda$, with $\mathfrak m_A\bar\Lambda=\mathfrak m_{A_0}\bar\Lambda=\bar{\mathfrak m}$ and residue field $F=F_1=F_0(\beta)\subseteq K$, finitely generated over $k$; as in the transcendental case, $k\to F$ is essentially of finite type [def-weil-pbc-essentially-finite-type-algebra] [def-weil-pbc-finite-type-algebra] and so is $k\to A$ [lem-weil-pbc-artinian-local-essentially-finite-type-residue]. So $A$ is admissible and $A_0\subseteq A$. Lift β⁻¹ through A → F to z ∈ A. Its residue is nonzero, so z is a unit of A. The residue of z x^Q - 1 in K is β⁻¹β - 1 = 0. It therefore belongs to m_B, and its n-th power is zero because m_B^n = 0. This supplies the required nilpotent error without capturing any actual power of x in A.

proof.text: In the algebraic case the residue field F of A is F₀(β), finite separable over F₀. The canonical differential isomorphism F ⊗[F₀] Ω[F₀/k] ≃ Ω[F/k] is supplied by [lem-weil-pbc-separable-algebraic-differentials-base-change], using Mathlib KaehlerDifferential.tensorKaehlerEquivOfFormallyEtale. Extend b₀ by scalars and transport it along this equivalence. The formula on 1 ⊗ dc_j identifies its vectors with d(residue_A(inclusion(a₀ j))). Take m = 0 and the empty family y. In the transcendental case use the polynomial-localization basis above with m = 1 and y₀ = x. Reindex the old and new vectors by Fin t₀ ⊕ Fin m; this also covers t₀ = 0.

theorem exists_popescu_unscaled_unit_basis
    (k : Type u) (Λ : Type v) [Field k] [CommRing Λ] [Algebra k Λ]
    [IsNoetherianRing Λ] (p : ℕ) [CharP k p] (hp : 0 < p)
    (q : Ideal Λ) [q.IsPrime] (n : ℕ) (hn : 1 ≤ n)
    (A₀ : Subalgebra k (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
      (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)) [IsLocalRing A₀]
    (hA₀ : A₀.IsPopescuAdmissible ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))).map
      (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n))))
    (t₀ : ℕ) (a₀ : Fin t₀ → A₀)
    (b₀ : Module.Basis (Fin t₀) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A₀)
      (KaehlerDifferential k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A₀)))
    (hb₀ : ∀ j, b₀ j = KaehlerDifferential.D k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A₀)
      (IsLocalRing.residue A₀ (a₀ j)))
    (s : Λ) (hs : s ∉ q) :
    ∃ (A : Subalgebra k (Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
        (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)) (_ : IsLocalRing A),
      ∃ hle : A₀ ≤ A,
      A.IsPopescuAdmissible ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))).map
        (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n))) ∧
      ∃ (Q : ℕ) (_ : 1 ≤ Q) (z : Aˣ),
        IsNilpotent (((z : A) : Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
            (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n) *
          (Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)
            (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) s)) ^ Q - 1) ∧
        ∃ (m : ℕ) (y : Fin m → A),
          (∀ j, (y j : Localization.AtPrime q ⧸
            (q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n) =
            Ideal.Quotient.mk ((q.map (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q))) ^ n)
              (algebraMap Λ (Localization.AtPrime q) s)) ∧
          ∃ b : Module.Basis (Fin t₀ ⊕ Fin m) (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
              (KaehlerDifferential k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)),
            (∀ j, b (Sum.inl j) = KaehlerDifferential.D k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
              (IsLocalRing.residue A (Subalgebra.inclusion hle (a₀ j)))) ∧
            (∀ j, b (Sum.inr j) = KaehlerDifferential.D k (IsLocalRing.ResidueField A)
              (IsLocalRing.residue A (y j)))
